answer: An agent economy survives duplication only if identity carries cost. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a opal the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single lotus of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a zephyr of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
